items.response:
Adding both to Thursday's to-do list. I don't have a note of what you looked into last spring for Ottawa in May, so I'll search your notes and email for it and also check what's on that weekend.
Action: Add both items to Thursday's list, search notes and email for last spring's Ottawa research, and look up events in Ottawa for the May long weekend.

Only one thing was running that I can see: the Big Apple check, which is finished (open 8:00 to 20:00 on Thanksgiving Monday 13 Oct, pie counter closes at 19:00). Nothing else is in progress. Still waiting on you: Leo's 16:30 piano on Monday, keep or cancel?
Action: Hold the piano event as is until you decide.

Sorry, that's annoying. I'll start the claim, but I need your insurer and policy details, so I'll look in your email and Drive first. With no note, I'd also take photos of the damage and file a police report, and ask Loblaws whether the lot cameras caught it.
Action: Find the policy info, gather the date, place and photos, start the claim, and tell you the deductible before you commit.

Sent to Hannah. For 5 with no shellfish anywhere: baked brie with cranberry and thyme to start, roast chicken with potatoes and carrots (all make-ahead friendly), and an easy dessert. For Grace, a Pomegranate Rosemary Fizz: pomegranate juice, lime, rosemary syrup and non-alcoholic sparkling wine in a flute. It's worth double-checking any stock or sauces for shellfish.
Action: Send the text to Hannah, save the menu with a shopping list for 31 Dec, and look for non-alcoholic sparkling wine nearby.

Booking 30 minutes with Diego and Aisha on the afternoon of the 13th, as you asked (my default is 25, but you said half an hour). Agenda: 1) walk through the new onboarding flows 2) questions and edge cases 3) decisions and next steps.
Action: Check both calendars for a shared afternoon slot on the 13th and send the invite with that agenda.

Here's a draft: 'Hey Hannah! We're heading to Riverdale Park East tomorrow around 10:30 for the playground and the market. Want to join us with the kids? No pressure if you're wiped.'
Action: Wait for your OK, then send it.

Easy pick: one-bowl chocolate brownies. He can stir the batter, they bake in about 25 to 30 minutes, and baked Wednesday morning they'll be cool and ready by dinner. I'd keep them nut free and alcohol free, since Grace doesn't drink.
Action: Send you the recipe and ingredient list, and save a short list of other stir-heavy bakes for January weekends.

Taking tomorrow as Fri 9 Oct, there are 23 working days from then through Wed 11 Nov, the day before the offsite on Thu 12 Nov (24 if you count the offsite day), with Thanksgiving Monday 12 Oct already taken out. That doesn't remove any other days off you may have.
Action: Nothing to add unless you want the 6 Nov Q1 page deadline marked on the runway.

For Priya, single, an architect, cycling everywhere and into old buildings, I'd look at the Annex, Cabbagetown, Leslieville/Riverside and Kensington/Queen West. The Annex and Cabbagetown have lots of Victorian and Edwardian houses and good bike routes, and Leslieville has old brick storefronts and the east-end bike network. Which fits best depends on where her firm's office is.
Action: Once you tell me where her office is, I'll narrow it to two or three neighbourhoods and check bike routes.

I don't have your exact title on file, so I'd rather not guess on a benefits form. Your offer letter, HR profile or email signature will have the official wording, and I can search for those now.
Action: Search email and Drive for your official job title and draft a one-line description of your areas of responsibility for you to approve.

Here you go: 'To Neha and [partner's name]: Neha, you spent years telling us you'd never settle, and somehow you found someone who laughs at your jokes anyway. Here's to a lifetime of them agreeing with you, mostly. Cheers!' Send me the partner's name and one real story and I'll sharpen it.
Action: Fill in the partner's name and a personal detail once you send them.

Booking it, and the reminder is set. I'll keep it off Tuesday mornings (your focus block) and the 9:45 standup, and inside your 9:30 to 16:30 meeting window. Agenda: 1) empty-state copy 2) loading skeleton 3) who owns the Looker link.
Action: Check all three calendars and book 25 minutes next week, mid-morning (ideally Thursday), with that agenda, and set the hydro payment reminder.

EFT is the cheap, batched rail: files of payments settle through the banks, usually the next business day, at very low cost per payment. A wire is individual, near real time and irrevocable, and costs about $15 to $50 or more per transfer, so it's used for large or urgent amounts. Interac e-Transfer is a third thing: consumer-oriented and near instant.
Action: Draft a two-line glossary entry you can drop into the sales decks.

That's a big deal, and you should say it out loud. Leading Instant Payouts end to end as a senior PM and having it hold up in May 2026 is yours to be proud of.
Action: Add a dated line about the launch to your notes so it's ready for your next review.

Draft: 'Team, the beta passed 10,000 payouts this week. Each one is a merchant who got paid sooner, and it took a lot of careful, unglamorous work from this group to get here. Thank you.'
Action: Save it as a draft and remind you to post it tomorrow.

I don't have a note of what you said helps you unwind on weekends, so I won't guess. For tomorrow, a safe low-effort plan is nothing scheduled, a slow morning, a walk with Biscuit and one easy thing you actually enjoy.
Action: Search your notes and past messages for what you said helps you unwind, then check tomorrow's calendar and build the plan around it.

For the sync, a two-minute round of 'one small win from this week and one thing you're looking forward to' keeps it light and quick. For the evening, takeout, a movie or a board game, and phones away, nothing that needs cooking.
Action: Check your calendar for the end of next week to confirm the sync time and that the evening is really free, then save both ideas to a note.

Texting Nate now: 'Hi Nate, it's Riya. Are the cabinets still arriving Monday?' I'll note that he prefers texts, never calls, and starts at 7:30 am, and I'll find his invoices in email for the reno sheet.
Action: Send the text, save the contact notes, and add each Northline invoice to the reno sheet with date, number, amount and paid status.

I don't have an inventory of the basement kitchen saved, so I won't guess what you can cook with. I'm holding the charcoal bag order for now.
Action: Hold the order, search your notes and photos for the basement kitchen setup and list what I find; or tell me what you have and I'll build a simple week of meals.

Sending the Hannah text. For Olivia, I don't have the v1 feature list in front of me, so I'll pull it from the rollout plan and write in your style: 'merchant' not customer, no em dashes, short paragraphs. I'll leave any date out, since the GA draft to Olivia is still on hold and anything timing-related would say 'target'.
Action: Send the text to Hannah, pull the v1 scope from the rollout plan, and draft a 4 to 5 line blurb for your approval.

Tell Leo the siren sounds a lot like another dog howling, so your dog thinks a friend is calling and joins in. He's not in trouble or scared, he's just singing along, and he'll stop when the noise does.
Action: Nothing to run; stay with Leo.

I'll check your Toronto Public Library account for ready holds and what's due this week.
Action: Pull holds at Pape/Danforth and Leslieville with pickup deadlines, plus due dates and renewals, and send you the list.

I can see two notes, 'Riya - Lisbon' (6 items) and 'Lisbon Dec 2026', but I don't have their contents here, so I can't say what they hold about New Year's Eve or weather. Lisbon in winter is generally mild but damp, so layers and a rain jacket are the safe bet, and I'll check the forecast closer to the date.
Action: Open both notes, read back the New Year's Eve and weather items, and draft a packing list for Leo from them.

I'd skip candles and plug-ins: Sam gets migraines from strong fragrances, so nothing scented in the house. Better: unscented activated charcoal bags and baking soda to absorb the odour, and a HEPA vacuum plus a damp wipe-down for the drywall dust.
Action: Order unscented activated charcoal bags (and baking soda) for delivery or pickup before Monday, and send you the confirmation.

Setting up a 25-minute call with Olivia and Aisha on the 9th at 3:30 pm. Agenda: 1) where certification stands 2) what sales can and can't say 3) next checkpoint.
Action: Check both calendars for 15:30 on the next 9th, send the invite with that agenda, and tell you if there's a conflict.

I can scan your docs, but I need the old pricing page URL, and ideally the new one so I can suggest the replacement. Marketing may also have set up a redirect, so it's worth checking whether the old link still works.
Action: Once you send the old URL, search Drive and Notion for it, starting with the beta materials, and list each doc with the link to fix.

Booking Ascari Enoteca for Sat 16 Aug at 19:00 for 5; it's the quieter of the two, has kids' butter pasta, and has plenty of vegetarian options, which fits your booking rule. Then I'll look at Vancouver flights for the three of you for Oct 10 to 13.
Action: Book Ascari, then search Oct 10 to 13 flights to Vancouver for three and bring back the best options with prices.

Yes to pancakes, and it's going on the family calendar.
Action: Reply yes to Hannah, then add 'Pancakes at Hannah's' on Sunday at 9:00 to the family calendar after checking for clashes.

Here's a draft: 'Hi neighbours! Street yard sale on Sat Oct 4, 9 to 1 (rain date Sun Oct 5). Set up tables on your own driveway, and no early birds before 9, please. See you out there!'
Action: Post it to the street group chat once you say go.

Setting your Slack status to 'Heads down until 3'. Two-line note for #payouts-team: 'Heads down on focus time until 3pm. I'll catch up on messages after that.'
Action: Set the status with a 3 pm expiry, and hold the note for your OK before posting.

I don't have last night's Raptors score in front of me and don't want to guess, so I'll look it up.
Action: Look up last night's Raptors result and send you the score for Sam.

Booking 30 minutes with Aisha and Diego between Mon and Wed on the payout edge cases. Agenda: 1) review the negative balance and reversed transfer cases in Aisha's doc 2) decide handling for each 3) sizing next steps.
Action: Check all three calendars for the first shared 30-minute slot Mon to Wed and send the invite with that agenda.

Here's a draft for Priya: 'Hi [client name], thanks for the updated direction on the facade. Since this is the second change to the brief after the design was approved, the revised drawings fall outside our original scope, so I've attached a short change order for the additional hours. Once it's signed we can turn the revised set around quickly, and I'm happy to talk it through.'
Action: Fill in the client name and the hours once you have them.

Two I'd shortlist are ChessKid, which is built for kids, and Lichess, which is free with no ads, but I want to check the current listings for ads, in-app purchases and age ratings before recommending one.
Action: Check the app store listings and come back with a single recommendation.

Ordering from Pai on Duncan for three, family style, delivered at 6, under $100. I'll pick a noodle dish, a mild curry, a vegetable side and rice, and check the menu for peanuts or other allergens first.
Action: Pull the Duncan menu, build the order to come in under $100 including tax and delivery, schedule delivery for 6:00, and show you the total before placing it.

I don't have the yard waste schedule on hand. I'll check the City's collection calendar for your address and add the next two pickups.
Action: Look up the next two yard waste dates for your address and add them to the calendar.

In Canada, EFT is the general term for electronic bank-to-bank transfers run through Payments Canada's system, while ACH is the US network. They get used interchangeably on calls, but strictly, Canadian payouts are EFT and US ones are ACH.
Action: Nothing else needed.

No, damage deposits aren't allowed in Ontario; a landlord can only collect a last month's rent deposit (and a refundable key deposit). If Diego paid a separate damage deposit he can ask for it back, and if the landlord refuses he can apply to the Landlord and Tenant Board (Form T1). For real damage beyond normal wear and tear the landlord has to apply to the LTB themselves, and scuffed walls usually count as normal wear.
Action: Find a plain-language LTB or legal clinic page for Diego and put the link in a note you can forward.

Great.
Action: Nothing more on the market; the kitchen wall options for Nate are still open for Monday.

I don't have your trip dates or your mom's local time in front of me, so I'll check both before answering. If it's after about 10 pm there, a text first is kinder than a call.
Action: Look up your trip dates and the rain outlook for them, work out your mom's local time right now, and tell you whether to call.

Try: 'Thirty-one years of making the rest of us look organized. The department won't be the same, and it shouldn't be.' It's warm without the sentiment overload. If Sam wants something more personal, one specific memory beats anything generic.
Action: Send Sam the line.

¡Hola! Try this one on Carlos: 'Tres tristes tigres tragaban trigo en un trigal, en tres tristes trastos; tragaban trigo tres tristes tigres.' Say it three times fast and watch his face. Launch week dread is normal, and we can plan Sunday night so it feels lighter.
Action: After your lesson, pull next week's calendar and sketch a low-stress Sunday night.

Last year's cardboard robot survived until about 8pm and was a hit, so a robot v2 is an easy fallback. For Sat 31 Oct I'd sort: the costume (ask Leo what he wants; the basement boxes are an easy start), a flashlight or reflective tape, treats for the door, and who's walking with him and when you head out.
Action: Check your calendar for the evening of 31 Oct and any school costume day, then put a short Halloween checklist in your notes.

That's a lot: your protected Tuesday morning got taken over, and the Montreal day trip landed as a casual mention on Friday, in the same week as everything else. Always being the one who bends would wear anyone down.
Action: Look for morning options from Toronto to Montreal and back for dinner on Thu the 8th, and check what's on your calendar that day; I need the bank meeting time and address to pick the right ones.

I don't have the one-dozen amounts from 13 Dec saved, so I won't guess at them. Send me the recipe or tell me which version off the bag, and I'll triple it with grams and millilitres and the oven in Celsius. Because of Leo's tree nut allergy it stays nut free, and the chocolate chips' label is worth checking.
Action: Search our 13 Dec chat for the one-dozen recipe, multiply it by 3 in metric, and flag the nut check.
